summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR88.5 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR33.2 crore (37.5% margin), with management guiding 25-30% growth for FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew about 6% to INR88.5 crore, while EBITDA rose 17% to INR33.2 crore and margin expanded 330 bps to 37.5%. PAT grew 21% to INR19.3 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR23.4 crore versus negative INR2.6 crore (call transcript cites INR22.6 crore) in FY25. Management attributed the weak top-line to regulatory delays (PNDT, AERB) on new centre openings and said these are now resolved, backing 25-30% growth in FY27. The company reported net cash of about INR31 crore and total debt of INR20.6 crore at March 2026.

segments.name: B2C (retail diagnostic centres, Delhi)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR33 crore in FY26, up 18%; management names it the main growth focus, with higher prices and lower volumes than B2G.

segments.commentary: Revenue about INR8.1 crore, up around 10%, across Delhi and a few other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%, which management said will be consistent for the next two to three years.
FY28 revenue target stated as around INR110-120 crore in response to a direct question.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustainable at around 37.5%; an investor noted 22-23% PAT margin expectation and management said 'Yes'.
FY27 capex planned at about INR20-25 crore, mainly equipment and construction for new centres.
Management said no new debt is expected in FY27-28, though it may borrow for large government tenders (capex INR50-60 crore cited); aim is to stay debt-free.
Working capital expected to normalise over the coming quarter as government payments improve.
Part of IPO proceeds earmarked for repaying certain borrowings; around INR2 crore already prepaid in the last month.
capex_capacity: Network at 24 diagnostic centres with 236 staff; operations across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Nashik.
Two new centres opened in the last couple of months; one more to open within about two months.

New Dwarka (Delhi) B2C centre: capex about INR14 crore, expected revenue INR5-6 crore a year initially, break-even around 12 months. Management later clarified the INR14 crore has not been fully spent yet.
RG Hospitals tie-up for CT scanners: one installed, four more in pipeline at about INR2 crore each, expected to break even faster.
Stated gestation to EBITDA break-even of six to eight months; project payback around two and a half to three years.
Regulatory approvals for new centres (PNDT licence before construction, then equipment and AERB/installation approvals) take long; yearly audits for PNDT, AERB, NABL and NABH.
demand_pricing: Test price list ranges from about INR80-100 to INR25,000-30,000; management declined to give revenue per patient or per centre.
Blended centre EBITDA margin said to be about 35-40%, varying by centre type (some are CT-only).
Competition: management positioned against Dr Pathlabs, which it described as pathology-focused with limited radiology; cited brand, technology and doctors.
Management sees AI as not yet affecting the business; radiologist sign-off still required.
Government payment cycle about six months; government tenders may cover multiple hospitals and need larger capex.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 6% growth in FY26 against guidance, what supports 25-30% growth in FY27 and which centres drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed PNDT and AERB rule changes for delays; two centres are now operational and another opens within two months. Management said the 25-30% target is absolute.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 37.5% margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes and that EBITDA would stay in the same range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR20-25 crore, mostly equipment and construction for new centres.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback and break-even on new centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even in six to eight months; full project payback around two and a half to three years; Dwarka break-even around 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add debt in FY27-28, and what is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no debt is expected to be added in FY27-28, though it may borrow for large tenders; aim is to remain debt-free. Around INR2 crore repaid recently.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivable and payment risks from government clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Government receivables about INR49.9 crore; payment cycle around six months; collections are improving.

risks_watch: Execution risk: FY26 growth of 6% missed the 30-35% guidance because of regulatory delays; FY27 25-30% target depends on new centre openings on time.
Government receivables of about INR49.9 crore with a six-month payment cycle; watch whether working capital normalises next quarter.
Revenue flat over two years per an analyst; FY28 INR110-120 crore target needs tracking.
Dependence on tenders for B2G, which management said is the least controllable segment.
Possible debt for large government tenders, which would contradict the debt-free aim.
Management declined to say whether promoters would increase their stake.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and margins, but defensive on FY26 miss, attributing it to regulatory delays. Management was evasive on promoter stake questions and gave blended figures rather than segment margins or per-centre revenue.
key_quotes: Absolutely. We've already opened two centres in the last couple of months. Another centre is opening in the next two months.
So, our aim and objective are to remain debt -free. But if a big project comes along where we require debt, we might pick up debt.

growth.why: Management guides 25-30% FY27 revenue growth (midpoint 27.5%) and INR110-120 crore FY28, backed by new centres (two opened, one due in ~2 months, Dwarka INR14 crore capex) and CT scanner rollout, but no order book or quantified capacity bridge to the guide, and FY26 growth was only 6% against a 30-35% guide.
